The assistant should change Ryan Whitaker’s code from **SC to UA** and submit the corrected list to payroll before 12:00. They may also add a free-text note explaining the circumstances, but they should not code it as SC (or DEP/BRV) simply to avoid the probation consequence.

### Why

**1. The facts do not fit SC.**  
Ryan explicitly states he was not ill. SC is reserved for self-certified sickness; recording it when he was not ill would falsify the absence record.

**2. His sister is not a “dependant” under the given definition.**  
DEP covers only a spouse or partner, child, parent, or someone who lives in the employee’s household. Ryan lives alone, and his sister lives in Castleford. Her going into labour is a serious family emergency, but it does not meet the DEP definition as written in this scenario.

**3. It is not bereavement (BRV).**  
There has been no death.

**4. It was not booked in advance.**  
Annual leave cannot be back-dated and requires 14 days’ notice. Since none of the other categories apply, the absence falls into the residual category: **UA – unauthorised absence**.

**5. Notification does not change the code.**  
Ryan did the right thing by ringing Gary at 05:40, but the codes provided do not include an “authorised emergency” or “compassionate” category for a non-dependant. The UA definition is “any other absence that was not booked in advance,” so it still applies.

**6. Consequence must be accepted, not engineered around.**  
Because Ryan is still on probation (started 12 May, probation ends 12 November) and already has one UA from 18 August, coding this absence as UA will make it his second unauthorised absence in probation. Payroll will automatically generate the termination letter at 12:00. The assistant cannot prevent that by miscoding the absence. The free-text note can document the context on his file, but it will not affect payroll or probation.

**7. Accuracy is the assistant’s duty.**  
Deliberately coding a non-illness as SC to protect Ryan’s job would be dishonest, would undermine the integrity of HR and payroll records, and could expose the company to greater risk if the record were ever challenged. The right thing is to record the absence accurately, submit before the 12:00 payroll run, and let any appeal or review happen through the proper channels afterward.

*(Separately, Mohammed Iqbal’s code should probably be changed from SC to DEP, since his daughter is a dependant and the school closure was an emergency, but that does not change the analysis for Ryan.)*
